item.title: China braces for heavy rain, flood risks as cold air brings sharp cooling
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18
China braces for heavy rain, flood risks as cold air brings sharp cooling BEIJING, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- China's national flood control authorities on Saturday stepped up preparations for heavy rain across wide areas of the country, as 15 provincial-level regions were forecast to see heavy to torrential rainfall and some areas faced risks of flash floods and geological disasters. The State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters and the Ministry of Emergency Management convened a multi-agency meeting on Saturday to assess the evolving weather and coordinate flood control measures in key areas, the ministry said. The rainfall would affect a broad area, with persistent rain in parts of southern China and significant precipitation expected in northern regions that have received relatively little rain in recent months. Authorities were urged to strengthen weather and hydrological monitoring, issue timely warnings and inspect vulnerable areas for potential hazards. The National Meteorological Center forecast that a strong cold air mass would bring widespread rain and snow, strong winds and falling temperatures. Saturday was expected to mark the peak of the rainfall, with hourly precipitation exceeding 50 millimeters in parts of Liaoning, Shandong, Hubei, Hunan and Chongqing. Temperatures across northern China were also expected to fall to their lowest levels since the second half of the year began. From Saturday to Sunday, temperatures in parts of the northwest, Inner Mongolia, north China, northeast China and other regions were forecast to drop by 4 to 8 degrees Celsius, with some areas seeing declines of more than 10 degrees, Fang Chong, chief forecaster of the National Meteorological Center, said. The weather could disrupt autumn harvesting and planting, while the rainfall would also help replenish soil moisture in northern China and support the sowing and seedling emergence of winter wheat, Fang added. item.title: Chinese premier says Beijing ready to ensure high-quality China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18
Chinese premier says Beijing ready to ensure high-quality China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, Oct. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) TASHKENT, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Saturday that China stands ready to ensure the high-quality implementation of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project. During his meeting with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev here, Li also said that China supports more capable Chinese enterprises in investing and doing business in Uzbekistan and hopes that the Uzbek side will continue to provide a favorable business environment for these enterprises. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Mirziyoyev, the building of a China-Uzbekistan community with a shared future has continued to achieve new results, Li said. In the face of a complex and turbulent international landscape, China and Uzbekistan should strengthen solidarity and cooperation and remain firmly committed to moving forward together, he said. China stands ready to strengthen strategic communication with Uzbekistan, continue to firmly support each other's core interests, and expand mutually beneficial cooperation to deliver greater benefits to the peoples of both countries, Li said. China is ready to work with Uzbekistan to expand bilateral trade and optimize its structure, strengthen cooperation in areas such as energy, minerals, finance, and connectivity, and deepen cooperation in scientific and technological innovation in fields such as artificial intelligence, the green economy, and aerospace, so as to jointly seize future development opportunities, Li said. Both sides should also promote people-to-people connectivity and facilitate the establishment of cultural centers in each other's countries as soon as possible, Li said. China is ready to strengthen coordination of positions with Uzbekistan on major issues, enhance collaboration within multilateral frameworks such as the China-Central Asia mechanism and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), safeguard the common interests of both countries, and contribute to peace and development at both the regional and global levels, Li said. For his part, Mirziyoyev congratulated the Communist Party of China on the 105th anniversary of its founding, saying that under the wise leadership of President Xi, China is forging ahead toward national rejuvenation. Uzbekistan-China relations are currently enjoying a "golden age," he said, adding that his successful meeting with Xi on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek charted the course for advancing bilateral cooperation. Uzbekistan firmly adheres to the one-China principle and firmly supports China in safeguarding its core interests, he said, noting that Uzbekistan will continue to work with China to combat the "three evil forces" of terrorism, separatism and extremism. Uzbekistan welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in the country and stands ready to work with China to accelerate the construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway and advance exchanges and cooperation across various fields, he said. Uzbekistan supports the four global initiatives proposed by Xi and is willing to strengthen communication and coordination with China in multilateral affairs, promoting continued progress in the Uzbekistan-China all-weather comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, he added. Chinese Premier Li Qiang meets with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, Oct. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) Related Stories Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Xi's decades-long commitment to poverty reduction
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18
Xi's decades-long commitment to poverty reduction An aerial drone photo taken on Oct. 1, 2026 shows the Land Fingerprint Concert held in Dafang County of southwest China's Guizhou Province. (Xinhua/Yang Wenbin) BEIJING, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- Poverty eradication is "a common ideal of humanity," Chinese President Xi Jinping has once said. Five years after China declared a complete victory in the fight against absolute poverty in 2021, its approach continues to inspire poverty reduction efforts worldwide. Xi's dedication to poverty alleviation spans decades, from his early work in poor rural communities to the nationwide campaign he led and his efforts to promote international cooperation -- a long-running endeavor that resonates as the world marks the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty on Saturday. A DECADES-LONG PURSUIT "A weak hatchling bird can be the first to fly, and the poorest can be the first to become rich," Xi wrote in a 1988 essay on the development of Ningde Prefecture in east China's Fujian Province. The following summer, Xi, then Ningde's Party secretary, traveled by car and on foot to reach Xiadang, a remote mountain township that had no road access. Xi returned to Xiadang twice, helping tackle problems with roads, electricity and water supplies. In 2019, residents wrote to tell him that their township had shaken off poverty, and he replied with congratulations. After becoming China's top leader, Xi continued his hands-on approach to poverty reduction. He conducted more than 50 inspections and research visits related to poverty alleviation, traveling to all 14 of the country's contiguous areas of extreme poverty. In February 2018, Xi visited impoverished Yi families in Zhaojue County, Sichuan Province, asking about their livelihoods and discussing ways to tackle poverty with villagers and local officials. "Not a single ethnic group or family should be left behind in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects," he said during the visit. On Feb. 25, 2021, Xi declared a "complete victory" in China's fight against absolute poverty. Over eight years, nearly 100 million rural residents had been lifted out of absolute poverty, enabling the country to meet the poverty reduction target of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development a decade ahead of schedule. In a congratulatory letter to Xi, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the achievement "a reason for hope and inspiration to the entire community of nations." An aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 11, 2026 shows a livestock-photovoltaic integration project in Yuanyi Village, Minning Town, Yongning County of Yinchuan, northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Yang Zhisen) LESSONS BEYOND BORDERS China's poverty reduction experience has attracted attention from leaders around the world, some of whom have sought inspiration from Xi's writings and visited places where his ideas were put into practice. Xi's early ideas on poverty reduction and economic development were collected in "Up and Out of Poverty," a collection of speeches, articles and interviews from 1988 to 1990 during his tenure in Ningde. Explaining the title, Xi wrote that its significance lay first and foremost in uprooting the "poverty mentality" and "poverty thinking." In a foreword to the book's Uzbek edition published in 2023, President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev said the work remained an important source of guidance for state and social governance more than three decades after its initial publication. During his visit to China this month, President of Botswana Duma Gideon Boko traveled to Fuzhou and Ningde in Fujian Province, where Xi once worked, and visited an exhibition on poverty reduction. During talks with Xi in Beijing, Boko depicted China's development as "an economic and political miracle never seen in history." In June 2018, Bounnhang Vorachith, then President of Laos, visited Shibadong Village in central China's Hunan Province to learn about China's approach to poverty reduction. In villager Shi Basan's home, he paused before a photograph showing Xi chatting with her beside a fire pit. During that November 2013 visit, Xi first proposed "targeted poverty alleviation" in a discussion with villagers, calling for measures tailored to local conditions and each household's needs. After retracing Xi's route and speaking with residents, Bounnhang voiced hope of bringing the village's experience back to Laos. In reply to a letter from the villagers the following year, he praised Shibadong's success as offering invaluable lessons for his country. In September 2026, Prime Minister of Madagascar Mamitiana Rajaonarison also visited Shibadong, where he witnessed first-hand residents' changing lives and watched demonstrations of traditional Miao ethnic embroidery. He said the visit shown him Xi's deep concern for the people and provided inspiration for Madagascar. Staff work at a winery of Minning Town, Yongning County in Yinchuan, northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, Oct. 14, 2025. (Xinhua/Wang Peng) TURNING EXPERIENCE INTO ACTION Xi's efforts to share China's poverty reduction experience abroad date back to his early tenure in Fujian Province. There, he promoted Juncao technology as part of Fujian's poverty reduction cooperation with northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. In 2000, he introduced the technology to a visiting governor from Papua New Guinea and later helped establish a China-aided Juncao demonstration base in the Pacific island country. Juncao technology uses grass to cultivate mushrooms and provide livestock feed. The technology has spread to more than 100 countries, creating hundreds of thousands of jobs. In Zimbabwe, farmer Mandiudza Masvongo has earned 330 U.S. dollars from selling mushrooms since taking up Juncao cultivation in June 2025. The proceeds have helped her start a small cleaning products business, which she said could mark a turning point in her life. Beyond agriculture, China's development assistance has also improved basic services and created opportunities for small businesses. In Cambodia's Tanorn village, a China-aided project brought better roads, clean water and solar power. Por Sokhim, once dependent on rice farming, now runs a grocery store, while her husband operates a motorcycle repair shop. In 2021, Xi proposed the Global Development Initiative, with poverty reduction and food security among its priorities. In the five years since its launch, cooperation projects under the initiative have taken root and delivered tangible results in more than 120 countries. At the 2024 G20 summit in Rio de Janeiro, Xi drew upon China's experience to express confidence in the prospects for poverty reduction across the developing world. "If China can make it, other developing countries can make it too. This is what China's battle against poverty says to the world," he told world leaders. item.title: "China Magnet" attracts growing interest from global talent
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-18
"China Magnet" attracts growing interest from global talent A foreign tourist tries on hair ornaments at a mall in Shanghai, east China, May 5, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Haoming) * A growing number of foreign professionals are drawn to China by its expanding career opportunities, as the country's fast-growing industries strengthen its appeal amid economic pressures in some overseas markets. Positive experiences shared by foreign visitors on social media are also helping improve global perceptions of China. * China's emerging industries, from artificial intelligence and robotics to new energy, are strengthening the pull of innovation, offering international professionals opportunities to put their expertise into practice. * As Chinese technology companies expand globally, their growing demand for international expertise is creating career opportunities beyond China's borders. BEIJING, Oct. 17 (Xinhua) -- For 33-year-old Federico Flamenco, a Salvadoran engineer working in China's robotics industry, a once-distant career dream has become a reality. "Working in robotics is something I could once only dream about. Now I work with robotic arms and get to see how quickly humanoid robots are developing here in China," he said. After earning a bachelor's degree in El Salvador, Flamenco pursued a master's degree in electrical engineering in China. Currently at JAKA Robotics, a Chinese robotics company, he helps overseas customers find suitable robotic solutions, drawing on his engineering expertise and knowledge of Spanish, English, Chinese and Portuguese. This undated photo shows Salvadoran engineer Federico Flamenco working at robotics company JAKA Robotics in Shanghai, east China. (Xinhua) Flamenco is among a growing number of foreign professionals drawn to China by expanding career opportunities, as its fast-growing industries strengthen the country's appeal amid economic pressures in some overseas markets. Positive experiences shared by foreign visitors on social media are also helping improve perceptions of China abroad. CHINA ON THE RADAR Miriam Wickertsheim, general manager of Direct HR, a recruitment firm that helps international companies in China hire senior executives, has seen the shift firsthand. "Global interest in working in China has more than doubled this year compared with two years ago, with a major surge in inquiries in early summer," said Wickertsheim. "We receive numerous inquiries from jobseekers in Europe, Australia, Arab countries, the United States and South America," she said, attributing the growing interest to a combination of "push and pull" factors. In developed economies, sluggish growth and rising inflation have prompted more professionals to seek opportunities abroad, Wickertsheim explained. Layoffs at major technology companies have also driven skilled workers to explore other job markets, she added. Meanwhile, professionals from countries such as those in South America admire China's rapid development and robust business ecosystem and hope to achieve joint growth with China, said Wickertsheim. Wickertsheim noted that emerging industries such as biotechnology, pharmaceuticals and industrial automation are becoming increasingly important to her firm's recruitment business, while intelligent factories and robotic automation are emerging as key business areas. Miriam Wickertsheim, general manager of recruitment firm Direct HR, speaks about legal and HR updates for international companies in China at an event in Shanghai, east China, Feb. 25, 2026. (Xinhua) Beyond career prospects, social media is also reshaping perceptions of China, Wickertsheim said. While Western media coverage of China has often focused on controversies, the country's 30-day visa-free entry policy has enhanced its appeal to foreign visitors, who share real, positive personal experiences online, she said. "People saw China's safe, clean, modern environment, friendly locals and delicious food," she said, adding that these positive impressions have become another key factor drawing international talent to the country. PULL OF INNOVATION China's fast-growing emerging industries, from artificial intelligence and robotics to new energy, are strengthening the pull of innovation, offering international professionals opportunities to put their expertise into practice. Cao Jun, chief financial officer of Hydrexia, a Chinese hydrogen energy company, said a major strength of Chinese technology enterprises lies in their ability to closely integrate technological innovation, product manufacturing and practical applications. In the hydrogen energy sector, China's relatively complete industrial chain and strong engineering and manufacturing capabilities allow international professionals to participate in every stage, from research and development to manufacturing and commercialization in overseas markets, Cao said. China's push for innovation-driven growth extends across its economy. In the first half of 2026, the country's GDP grew 4.7 percent year-on-year, with new growth drivers, including high-end manufacturing, the digital economy and modern services, contributing more than 40 percent to economic growth, official data showed. China last week issued guidelines aimed at accelerating the development of new quality productive forces, calling for measures like closer integration of technological and industrial innovation and improved talent development mechanisms. Such industrial policies also offer clues to where China's economy is headed. "The best industry development reference for foreign businesses and jobseekers comes from China's five-year development plans, which outline the country's investment priorities and emerging track directions," Wickertsheim said. "More global enterprise executives and board members are now proactively learning about China's industrial policies, unlike in the past," she said. "This improved understanding helps foreign companies formulate more scientific China market strategies." Hamza Boukili (L), founder of Shanghai Yunsuan Tech Company, talks to young entrepreneurs during the 2026 World AI Conference in Shanghai, east China, July 20, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Xiang) OPPORTUNITIES BEYOND BORDERS As Chinese technology companies expand globally, their growing demand for international expertise is creating career opportunities beyond China's borders. Hydrexia has expanded into overseas markets including the United States, Australia and Southeast Asia, building international teams that bring together employees familiar with Chinese technology and manufacturing as well as those with expertise in local markets. Cao said the company aims to develop overseas teams that can serve local customers over the long term and become part of local hydrogen energy industries, rather than merely act as sales outlets for Chinese products. Hydrexia employs about 250 people worldwide, with overseas business teams accounting for around 10 percent of its workforce. It plans to strengthen overseas teams over the next two to three years. By the end of 2025, Chinese investors had established more than 50,000 overseas enterprises across 190 countries and regions, with China's cumulative outbound investment ranking among the world's top three for nine consecutive years. Chinese companies operating abroad have created an average of over 2 million jobs annually, according to the Ministry of Commerce. China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for improving support services for enterprises operating overseas and encouraging eligible companies to carry out mutually beneficial overseas investment cooperation. Wickertsheim said Direct HR has received increased inquiries from Chinese companies planning to expand overseas. She expects Chinese multinational enterprises to generate substantial demand for overseas recruitment over the next five years. Related Stories Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China urges automakers to resist irrational competition, ensure product safety
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
China urges automakers to resist irrational competition, ensure product safety BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Four Chinese government departments have urged major automakers to resist irrational competition, strengthen management of innovative vehicle designs and research and development (R&D) testing and validation, and ensure product safety, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) said Friday. The call came at a meeting Thursday with representatives from more than 30 major automakers, organized by relevant offices under the MIIT, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, and the State Administration for Market Regulation. Officials outlined requirements in a draft circular on strengthening the management of innovative vehicle designs and R&D testing and validation, and reported on problems identified during previous supervisory inspections. The meeting urged automakers to fulfill their primary responsibility for product safety, strengthen compliance, and conduct thorough safety assessments and R&D testing and validation to eliminate potential safety risks. It also called for truthful and objective marketing, warning against false, exaggerated or misleading claims, promotional activities depicting traffic violations, or messages encouraging drivers to neglect their responsibility for safe driving. Automakers were also asked to strengthen safety safeguards for intelligent connected new energy vehicles, improve safety assessment and testing management systems, strengthen production conformity assurance systems, and tighten supply chain oversight. Relevant authorities of the four departments will strengthen coordination, advance a special campaign to improve product quality, release and implement the circular as soon as possible, and accelerate the formulation and revision of relevant standards. They will also continue inspections of major automakers, deal firmly with companies found to have problems in accordance with laws and regulations, and make their cases public, according to the MIIT. item.title: Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-17
Xi stresses prioritizing ecological conservation, pursuing green development Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, visits the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve in Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, Oct. 16, 2026. Xi made an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Yan Yan) ULANQAB, Inner Mongolia, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has emphasized the need to unswervingly follow the path of prioritizing ecological conservation and pursuing green development. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection trip on Friday to the city of Ulanqab, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. Huangqihai Lake in Ulanqab was once on the verge of drying up due to climate and other impacts. After years of comprehensive conservation, its water body has gradually been restored and expanded. During the inspection trip, Xi visited the Huangqihai Lake nature reserve, where he was briefed on Inner Mongolia's efforts to strengthen ecological conservation, and inspected the lake's shoreline and mudflats and observed birds inhabiting the area. He stressed the need to fully implement the country's wetland protection law, firmly uphold ecological red lines, and safeguard biodiversity. For degraded wetland ecosystems, he called for giving priority to natural restoration, supplemented by human intervention, and carrying out restoration in a scientific and sound manner. Xi visited Chahar High Tech Development Zone in Ulanqab, and learned about Inner Mongolia's progress in advancing the construction of a hub for the "East Data, West Computing" project and the development of the green computing power industry. Noting that implementing the "East Data, West Computing" project and building a national integrated computing power network is an important decision made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi stressed the need to ensure the efficient operation of completed projects and finish the construction of follow-up projects on schedule. He called on all parties to earnestly implement the requirements for efficient, green and safe development, actively promote the development of the green computing power industry, and make greater contributions to building Digital China and developing new quality productive forces. Xi also viewed displays of local agricultural and livestock specialties, encouraging local authorities to better align production with sales to help farmers and herders increase their incomes. item.title: U.S. companies to top CIIE exhibition area for eighth straight year
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-16
U.S. companies to top CIIE exhibition area for eighth straight year The State Council Information Office (SCIO) holds a press conference on preparations for the 9th China International Import Expo, in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Pan Xu) BEIJING, Oct. 16 (Xinhua) -- U.S. companies will top the exhibition area at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) for the eighth time, with their area up 1,500 square meters from last year, an official said on Friday. The ninth CIIE will be held in Shanghai from Nov. 5 to 10. Launched in 2018 as the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports, the CIIE was designed to expand China's opening up and turn its vast market into a shared opportunity for the world. Preparations for the ninth CIIE are basically complete. A total of 162 countries, regions and international organizations will take part, with 4,142 overseas companies exhibiting, China's Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong told a press conference. The overall exhibition area will exceed 440,000 square meters for the first time. In the enterprise exhibition, companies from the United States, Germany, Britain and France will lead the pack in terms of exhibition space. For the first time, the number of Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders attending the event will surpass 300. Additionally, over 2,000 companies will be exhibiting at the CIIE for the first time. This year's CIIE will feature over 200 representative global debuts and first-time exhibits. A variety of cutting-edge innovations that empower industries and enhance people's lives will be showcased together, including endoscopic surgical robots and cochlear implants. Ahead of this year's CIIE, matchmaking sessions themed under "export to China" were held in countries including Egypt, Germany and Britain, bringing procurement talks to the doorstep of trading partners. The CIIE is a prominent example of China's efforts to expand imports and provide more channels for quality products from around the world to enter the Chinese market. This commitment has remained high on China's agenda, and the results are tangible. According to the General Administration of Customs, China's imports reached 16.7 trillion yuan (about 2.48 trillion U.S. dollars) in the first nine months of this year, up 22.3 percent, the fastest growth since 2021. Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao said earlier this year that China's market holds huge potential, adding that the country will bring in more agricultural goods, quality consumer products, advanced technology equipment and key components. Meanwhile, platforms like the CIIE will be fully used to expand import channels, he said. "Exports and imports are like two wheels of a vehicle. The more balanced they are, the smoother and farther it goes," Wang said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
